text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 6.3% today as oil prices surged on geopolitical tension—U.S. crude climbed to $96 per barrel while Brent crude hit nearly $114, driven by escalating U.S.-Iran conflict and threats of new strikes in the Middle East. For a major U.S. refiner, higher crude prices can initially boost margins if they can pass costs to consumers, and tightening global supply has refineries running at 92.5% capacity with diesel inventories at historically low levels.

The backdrop amplifies the move: Europe is facing a diesel crisis and urging the U.S. to release reserves, while tariff threats against countries buying Russian oil are tightening supply further. This supply squeeze—combined with refineries already running near full capacity—creates the conditions where a refiner with U.S. coastal assets benefits from both higher oil prices and stronger demand for refined products like diesel.
